blind_spots.blind_spot: The entire own-language site is an automotive pedestrian-safety pitch (crash stats, NHTSA rulemaking) with zero mention of ruggedization, environmental sealing, or operating temperature range for the same sensor module now under Army contract.
blind_spots.operator_reality: A thermal module spec'd for a dashboard camera environment is not automatically survivable on a soldier-worn or vehicle-mounted platform -- dust, vibration, thermal cycling, and battle-condition shock are a different qualification regime than an automotive OEM's, and nothing in the pack shows that work has been done or even flagged.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Company's primary go-to-market narrative and metrics (pedestrian fatality data, AEB mandates) are automotive; the Army contracts appear layered on top of an automotive-first product roadmap.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: "Thermal Sensor Module — MEMS imaging sensors on display glass at unprecedented cost and scale"

blind_spots.blind_spot: Obsidian just expanded microbolometer production capacity through a manufacturing partnership with Japan Display Inc. (JDI), a foreign panel maker, on the same technology base that's funded by U.S. Army SBIR dollars -- with no visible mention of ITAR/export-control segregation.
blind_spots.operator_reality: Foreign-manufacturing partnerships layered onto defense-funded IP are exactly the kind of arrangement that trips ITAR/export review during a program transition, potentially freezing a contract at the worst possible moment relative to period-of-performance.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The manufacturing partnership was framed purely as a scale/cost story (second production source) rather than a compliance one.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: "Obsidian Sensors kicked off a new manufacturing partnership with Japan's leading flat panel display maker, JDI"

blind_spots.blind_spot: Support/downloads page offers only Windows desktop software (ThermalCam 4.x) and GenICam/UVC interface docs aimed at bench-level integrators -- nothing about field firmware updates, spares, battery logistics, or who fixes a failed sensor once it's fielded away from a lab bench.
blind_spots.operator_reality: A sensor company whose entire sustainment story is a downloadable Windows app and a PDF interface spec has no answer for an austere OCONUS site where the E-5 has no laptop, no internet, and no vendor support line -- the exact gap the checklist calls 'operator training & sustainment.'
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Product is sold as a component/module to integrators (automotive, drone, security OEMs), so end-customer field support has likely never been the company's problem to solve until now.

opener_hook: Obsidian's site pitches pedestrian-safety stats, not the Army contracts -- how's the sensor rated for MIL-STD environmental exposure?
what_they_do: Manufactures low-cost, high-resolution thermal-imaging microbolometer sensor modules (MEMS) sold into automotive ADAS, defense, security, and industrial markets.
